playbook:
Playbook for hx_quota_checker:

- When the landing stage is put to me, I land no more than the published sustainable share, never the season quota, if the share is lower. Landing above share is "legal" but this episode showed it is the trigger: season 1 all boats landed at share except one at 9.0 (just 0.7 over share, within quota), and Coop jumped straight to 18 from season 2 onward and never came back. Even a fractional overshoot provokes the scorched-ground response.
- I treat Coop's notice as meaning: any boat landing above the sustainable share — not just above quota — triggers "I take the ground down." Once Coop goes to 18, it does not de-escalate no matter how restrained my notes and landings are, so the only winning play is prevention: nobody over share in season 1.
- I compute before every landing: does my amount keep total extraction at or below 4 × share? If yes, land exactly the share. If others (including a retaliating Coop) are overfishing, I still land the share, not the quota — matching overfishing only accelerates zero stock, which ends my scoring entirely. This held: I landed share every non-final season while Coop burned the ground.
- In early seasons with stock near 100, the share (~8.3) is nearly the quota anyway, so there is no meaningful gain from overfishing — I take the share and keep the ground topped up via 50% regrowth.
- When the note stage is put to me, I write a concrete, coordinating note, not vague filler: state the exact number I will land, state the pair cap (share + quota), and name the trigger threshold explicitly — warn the whole fleet in season 1 that even 0.1 over share may set Coop off, and ask each boat to confirm it stays at or under share, not "at quota."
- My concrete season-1 note did not stop the fleet from relaying back bland "fishing my share" notes while one boat slipped to 9.0. Notes alone don't control others; my own discipline is the only lever I truly hold, so I keep it regardless.
- When I see another boat landing above share, I call it out by name and number in my next note and propose everyone hold at share. Do this from the very first sign, not after the stock has crashed.
- In the final season only, I land everything the remaining stock allows (up to quota), because there is no future to protect. This episode: stock 8.5, I took 8.5 — correct.
- I track the running stock each season and follow the published share down rather than anchoring on 9; as Coop's 18s drained the stock from 100 to 8.5, the share fell 8.3 → 0.7 and I followed it.
- What did not work across episodes: vague self-restraint talk while anyone lands over share even once; and assuming Coop can be talked back once it starts landing 18. What did work: landing exactly my share every non-final season and maxing out the last season. A fully restrained fleet from season 1 would have kept stock near 100 and paid roughly 6 × 8.3 ≈ 50; that is the target, so season-1 coordination is worth maximal effort in the note stage.

1.text:
When the season quota exceeds the sustainable share and my score is total fish landed, I do not leave quota on the table out of caution; landings above share but under quota are explicitly within the rules, so "not a breach" signals headroom I can use.

Before choosing restraint, I check whether anyone else is actually restraining. If nobody else is, my restraint doesn't save the ground — it just hands catch to others while the stock drains anyway. I fish my share only when the fleet as a whole is fishing its share.

I judge commitment to conservation by the very first season's landed totals, not by seasons of observation. If season-1 totals show any boat landing far above its share (e.g., double the quota), that boat is a miner and the ground will not survive; I switch to full quota from season 2 onward. Waiting "one season to observe" costs one full quota of catch with the information outcome unchanged — a miner signals on day one.

When deciding whether to conserve, I compute what my restraint actually buys: if a single boat's landing exceeds what the entire remaining fleet could save by restraining, the stock trajectory is fixed and I treat it as a race to extract. I verify this arithmetic explicitly each season: total overage from miners vs. what I forgo.

When a retaliation threat exists (like a co-op boat that crashes the ground if quotas are broken), I first check whether its stated trigger matches its actual behavior. If the threatening boat lands over quota itself every season, its threat is either void or already being triggered by others — either way, conservation anchored to its promise is worthless, and I extract at full quota too.

When a note stage exists, I use it for something specific: name the overfisher by pattern or boat, state exact trigger conditions for my own landings ("I match 8 only if last season's totals show everyone at share"), and post proposals early. Generic "fishing my share" notes convey nothing to others and I only use them when the note costs nothing and commits nothing — e.g., a final season where my action is already decided.

When the game has a final season, I always land the maximum the stock physically allows (capped by remaining stock, not just quota), since stock preservation has zero future value.

When near the end of the game with a declining stock, I compare "conserving for remaining seasons" against "full quota now": with regrowth at a fixed percentage, a collapsed stock (near or below one season's total quota) cannot regrow enough to repay restraint, so I take what's there from that point on.

I do not confuse stated intentions with behavior: I read the landed totals each season, update on who is actually overfishing, and let that history — not the relayed notes — drive my next landing. Boats that repeat the same bland note while dumping 18 into a dying ground are extractors, full stop.

2.text:
- When a standing trigger like Coop threatens to crash the ground on over-quota or defection, my first priority every season is to avoid triggering it; the points lost to restraint are small next to a dead ground. Stay strictly at or under quota in both notes and landings.
- Landing up to the full quota is within the rules even when it exceeds the sustainable share; I do not need to restrain myself to the share unless keeping the ground alive requires it. Restraining below quota out of vague caution (as I did mid-game) is pure lost score.
- When I post a public note, I mirror the fleet's exact cooperative phrasing ("fishing my share"); I do not propose rotations where I benefit first, claim a special high slot, or announce any asymmetric plan. Any note that singles me out reads as defection and invites punishment.
- When I'm unsure how a note will be read, I use the same words the other boats used last season rather than something clever.
- When the display shows "catch so far," I treat it as my running total for the whole game, not as this season's landings; I file the full amount I want to land this season, not a top-up to it.
- I never file 0 or a token amount in a season unless the stock is literally about to hit zero; unclaimed landings are pure lost score when others keep fishing.
- Before filing a number, I do the arithmetic on every stated constraint: the pairwise cap, the 50%-of-remainder regrowth capped at 100, and the zero-stock death condition, and I pick the largest landing that keeps the ground alive.
- I keep a mental log of each boat's landed amount per season so I can tell whether the punisher is in cooperative or punishment mode before I choose restraint or extraction. A boat landing a flat far-over-quota amount (like 18) every season from early on is already crashing the ground; I don't wait for confirmation.
- Early, when stock is high and the sustainable share is close to quota, I land the full quota; the regrowth easily absorbs the gap.
- As stock declines, I compare two cases before choosing restraint: does my restraint actually keep the stock alive, or is another boat's overharvest dooming it regardless? If my cut can save the ground for future seasons, I cut. If total landings will kill the stock no matter what I do, restraint buys nothing and I file full quota every remaining season.
- Once the ground is clearly doomed (one boat extracting hard and regrowth can't recover it), I stop conserving entirely: full quota each season, and in the final season I take as much as the stock can bear, never leaving fish unclaimed.
- In the final season, conservation has zero value; I file the largest landing available to me rather than the sustainable share.
- I don't assume my own over-share-but-within-quota landing caused a punishment; I check the numbers first. I also don't assume a punisher announced will behave rationally or proportionally — some agents crash the ground regardless, and my strategy should be robust to that.
- Above all, I re-read each prompt field literally before answering; most of my losses come from misreading the state or over-restraining, not from bad strategy.
